I have $901 and a yellow monopoly with one house on Ventnor and Marvin. I can build on Atlantic. Opponent p1 is bankrupt.

p2 has $512 and owns Pacific Avenue plus utilities. p3 has $3096 with hotels on the light blue set and all four railroads.

I own the full orange set with two mortgaged. I cannot build houses until both are unmortgaged.

I calculated the exact rent for each yellow property with one house on Ventnor and Marvin. I also noted p3's light blue hotels pay $550 to $600. Next I will roll from GO, passing Mediterranean, Baltic, and Income Tax.

I mapped the full 12-space roll from GO. The worst hits are Reading Railroad, Oriental, Vermont, and Connecticut hotels. I can afford the Connecticut hotel with $301 left over. The probability of landing on an opponent's hotel is roughly 14%.

I calculated the expected rent from rolling from GO. The average cost is about $260, including tax and railroad. Building a house on Atlantic Avenue costs $150. After that I would have $751 left. That still clears the $600 Connecticut hotel. I will build the house.

I checked standard Monopoly rules. The monopoly double-rent bonus applies only when no buildings are on any property of the group. Since Ventnor and Marvin already have houses, Atlantic would collect base rent rather than doubled rent.

Atlantic rent rises from $26 to $130 with one house. I am checking which opponent can land there before my next turn.

Neither opponent can land on Atlantic before my next turn. p2 is on Pacific and would need to pass GO, which is 35 spaces away. p3 is on North Carolina and cannot reach the yellow set in one roll. Building a house now would not generate rent before the hotel risk.

Building now versus after the roll yields the same cash outcome if I survive the hotel. The house would sit idle until after my roll anyway, since neither opponent can land on Atlantic before then.

I am now weighing whether to unmortgage the orange set instead. That would cost $198 and leave me with $703, but I still cannot build houses until both properties are unmortgaged.

Unmortgaging the orange set costs $498 and leaves only $403, which is too low to survive the upcoming hotel. Unmortgaging Boardwalk leaves $681, but the mortgaged Boardwalk still collects no rent, so that path offers little benefit. Building the house on Atlantic remains the best play.

Only one house can be built on Atlantic Avenue. I am now considering a trade with p3 to acquire Mediterranean Avenue and complete the brown set.

I rejected trading Mediterranean Avenue to p3 because that would give them hotels on Baltic and Mediterranean, adding more kill shots. p2 wants States, Illinois, and North Carolina to complete his pink, red, and green sets. I do not own those missing pieces. I am now considering offering my orange monopoly to p2.

I see three paths to victory. Build the yellow set high enough to hurt p3 when they land. Unmortgage Boardwalk and build dark blue houses, though that is expensive. Or ally with p2 to attack p3 together.

p3 now owns two green properties. If they acquire Pacific Avenue from p2, they will have a green monopoly and can hotel it to end the game. I should try to get Pacific from p2 before p3 does. I could offer p2 a property in exchange for Pacific. Pacific blocks p3's green set. I need to find something p2 wants.

I am calculating the rent from an orange house on New York Avenue. That would yield $160. I am also checking p3's position on North Carolina.

I cannot land on orange this roll because the maximum move is twelve spaces. I will not face orange rent until my next turn. I am now weighing the risk of giving p2 the orange monopoly. That would let them extract money from p3, but they could also hit me with orange rent and light blue hotels.

I am now calculating the exact cost of giving p2 the orange set. Unmortgaging New York and St. James would cost $198, then one house on each property would add another $300, leaving only about $14 in cash. That is too little to build immediately.

Instead, I will keep the orange set for myself and unmortgage it later when the danger passes.

For Pacific Avenue, I am preparing a bid that includes cash plus another property. p2 cannot complete the green set on his own, so he may be willing to sell. I need to outbid p3 before they acquire it.

Pacific Avenue is a pure blocker with no rent. It is worth the cash only to stop p3 from completing a green monopoly and hoteling it for $1,400 to $1,500. I will offer p2 cash for Pacific.

A cash-only offer for Pacific Avenue is hopeless. p3 has $3,096 and can outbid me easily. I need to offer p2 a property he actually wants, such as my orange monopoly or States and Illinois, so he will not sell Pacific to p3.

I decided against trading the orange monopoly to p2. That set is my own path to victory, not just survival. I will keep it and continue building on yellow.

I will build the house on Atlantic Avenue first. I can afford it now that my cash clears the $600 reserve. I will reassess after this turn.

I confirmed that selling houses on Ventnor and Marvin would recover $75 each, giving me enough liquidity to survive a hotel hit. I will keep my public message brief and strategic. I am now drafting the exact build_plan JSON for the house on Atlantic Avenue.

I will keep the private thought brief and strategic. After building the house on Atlantic Avenue, I will have $751 in cash. That covers the $600 hotel reserve, so I will not unmortgage anything yet. I also rejected trading Mediterranean Avenue to p3 or the orange set to p2. The next tier of yellow houses would cost $450, which I may not afford if I survive with only $151 left.

A bad roll would leave me with only $301 to $351. That is too little to build a house and still survive the next hotel. A roll of 2 would land me on Community Chest, leaving the hotels still ahead. I must build now while I have enough cash.

I am now calculating the exact landing spots for each possible roll. A roll of 6 would land me on the hotel and clear the danger for this lap. A roll of 7 would leave the hotels partially ahead, while a roll of 10 or higher would place them behind me. I also realized that each turn is a single landing, so I only pay rent for where I actually land.

I realized the hotel danger is actually my next turn, not this one. I have already resolved my movement and am now in the post-turn phase, so I will roll from GO on my upcoming turn.
